entries.title: Files attached to sub-sessions now sync to Swapcard
entries.summary: When **Sessions 2.0** sub-sessions are enabled and **Sync sub-sessions** is on, files attached to a sub-session are now included in the Swapcard content sync alongside parent-session files. Previously, only parent-session files were sent, so sub-session files never appeared as Swapcard documents. Existing sub-session files will attach to their Swapcard planning entry on the next sync.

enable.path: Apps → Swapcard → Event Settings → Sync sub-sessions

entries.use_case: An organizer using Swapcard with a multi-part session structure can now upload presentation files to individual sub-sessions in Sessionboard and have them appear correctly on each sub-session's Swapcard planning entry, without any manual workaround.

cs_action.note: Customers using Swapcard with Sessions 2.0 sub-sessions who reported missing files on sub-session plannings should be told to run a manual sync on the parent session to pick up any files uploaded before this fix.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that files added to sub-sessions are not showing up in Swapcard, or that sub-session plannings are missing documents.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using the Swapcard integration with Sessions 2.0 sub-sessions who attaches files to individual sub-sessions.
internal.staff_path: Apps → Swapcard → Sync (trigger a sync on the parent session to backfill existing sub-session files)
internal.gotchas: Files uploaded to sub-sessions before this fix will only appear in Swapcard after the next sync of the parent session. Files in quarantine are still sent to Swapcard (parity with parent files); a follow-up ticket covers that gap.
internal.talk_track: Files you attach to sub-sessions in Sessionboard now flow through to Swapcard automatically on the next sync, so attendees see the right materials on each part of a multi-part session.

draft.docs_gap: The Swapcard integration guide should note that sub-session files are included in the content sync when Sessions 2.0 and Sync sub-sessions are enabled, and that a manual "sync this session" on the parent is needed to attach pre-existing sub-session files.

entries.title: Slide video titles and chat timing are now accurate
entries.summary: Two defects in the slide video editor are fixed. Slides whose first line was a letter-spaced kicker (e.g. **W H E R E W E S TA R T E D**) now show a readable title drawn from the first real line of text. When you ask the **Edit by asking** chat to place a slide at an exact time such as 1:00, it places it at exactly 1:00 and confirms in one plain sentence — it no longer snaps to the nearest transcript line or show its reasoning.

where.path: Marketing → Media → [recording] → Slide video → Edit by asking

entries.use_case: An organizer editing a slide video no longer has to guess which slide is which when kicker text was letter-spaced in the original deck, and can confidently say "bring slide 4 in at 1:00" knowing the chat will honour that exact time.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports garbled slide titles in the slide video editor or complains that the chat moved a slide to the wrong time.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using slide videos with decks that have letter-spaced kicker text, or who uses the chat to set precise slide timings.
internal.gotchas: The title fix is display-only; the underlying alignment data is unchanged. The chat timing fix applies only when the user states an exact time — 'when they talk about X' still anchors to the transcript.
internal.talk_track: Slide titles in the editor now read as real words even when the original deck used letter-spaced headings, and the chat places slides at exactly the time you ask for.

draft.docs_gap: The guide's "Edit by asking" section should note that exact times (e.g. 1:00) are placed as given, and that slide titles are derived from the first readable line of text rather than the raw PDF output.

entries.title: Platform Awards programs block new starts and submissions after the close date
entries.summary: Once an Awards program's close date passes, submitters can no longer start a new submission or submit a completed one. Attempts after the deadline are refused. This reverses the previous behaviour (SB-9471) that allowed late submissions.
entries.use_case: Organisations that set a firm submission deadline can now trust that no entries slip through after the close date, keeping the competition fair without manual intervention.

cs_action.note: This reverses SB-9471. Any customer who relied on accepting late submissions after the close date will now see those attempts blocked. Reach out to Awards customers who have active programs with close dates in the near term.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When an Awards customer asks why submitters can no longer submit after the close date, or when setting up a new program with a firm deadline.
internal.who_should_get_it: All Platform Awards customers — this is on by default.
internal.gotchas: This is a breaking change from SB-9471. Customers who previously relied on late submissions being accepted will be affected immediately. There is no flag to revert to the old behaviour.
internal.talk_track: Your Awards program now enforces its close date automatically — once the deadline passes, no new submissions can be started or completed, so your competition stays fair without any manual policing.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that once the program close date passes, submitters cannot start or complete a submission, and that this is enforced automatically.

entries.title: Marketing Pages: sign-up form and premiere blocks, translated UI, and on-demand library controls
entries.summary: In **Marketing › Pages**, the **Add block** menu now includes a **Sign-up form** block and a **Premiere** block. Website snippets and form questions display in the admin's language (German, Spanish or French). An on-demand library can now be **Unpublished** or **Deleted** from its page, each behind a confirmation dialog.
entries.use_case: A marketing admin working in Spanish or French now sees page builder snippets and form questions in their own language, and can add a sign-up form or premiere block directly from the page editor without leaving the builder. They can also take an on-demand library offline or remove it entirely when a campaign ends.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Marketing beta customer asks about adding sign-up forms to pages, managing on-demand libraries, or reports that the page builder shows English text despite their admin language being set to German, Spanish or French.
internal.who_should_get_it: All Sessionboard Marketing beta customers, especially those with non-English admins.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Pages → (open or create a page) → Add block
internal.gotchas: Translated UI applies to self-serve Marketing orgs only; a Platform org with a de/es/fr admin still sees English in the page builder. The sign-up form block requires web-api round 6 and org-portal to be deployed after web-api (capture forms send `lng`).
internal.talk_track: You can now drop a sign-up form or a premiere directly onto any page, and the whole builder reads in your language. When a campaign wraps up, unpublish or delete the on-demand library right from its page.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the Sign-up form block and Premiere block options in Add block, explain how to unpublish or delete an on-demand library, and note that snippets and form questions display in the admin's configured language.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing Pages let you publish event landing pages, sign-up forms and on-demand libraries without a separate website tool. You control the layout with blocks, apply your brand kit, and connect registration directly to the page. Use it to launch a campaign page, collect email sign-ups before tickets go on sale, or host a post-event on-demand library for attendees.

entries.title: Marketing pages, emails, exports and checkout follow the event or admin's language
entries.summary: For Sessionboard Marketing workspaces, event pages now start in the event's language, with capture-form copy, consent text, thank-you text and the double opt-in email and confirmation page all matching the visitor's language. **People** and **Results** CSV exports use column headers in the admin's language. Stripe Checkout displays in the org's language with a line describing what the customer is buying. Newsletter archive and issue pages, the shared **Results** link, engagement milestones and the library gate also follow the org's or admin's language.
entries.use_case: An organizer running a German-language event can publish a registration page, send a double opt-in email and export their contacts list entirely in German, without any manual copy-and-paste of translated text.

cs_action.note: Applies automatically to self-serve Marketing workspaces; no flag to flip. Platform orgs are unaffected — their CSV headers remain English regardless of admin language.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a self-serve Marketing customer asks about running a non-English event or complains that their exported CSV headers are in English.
internal.who_should_get_it: Self-serve Marketing customers whose events or audiences are primarily German, Spanish or French.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Pages (event page builder) / People → Export / Results → Export
internal.gotchas: Translated CSV headers apply to self-serve orgs only. A Platform org with a de/es/fr admin still gets English CSV headers — this is intentional and tested. Stripe Checkout language follows the org's language setting.
internal.talk_track: Your event pages, sign-up forms, confirmation emails and exported reports now appear in your event's language automatically — no copy-pasting translations needed.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that the page builder automatically starts new event pages in the event's language and that capture-form copy, consent text, double opt-in emails and CSV export headers all follow the event's or admin's language for self-serve workspaces.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing lets you promote events, collect sign-ups and distribute content from a single workspace. When your audience speaks German, Spanish or French, every touchpoint — registration pages, confirmation emails, opt-in flows, exported reports and checkout — reflects that language automatically, so visitors see a consistent experience and your team gets reports they can read without translation.

entries.title: Event pages and video gates follow the page's language for labels and consent
entries.summary: On a Sessionboard Marketing event page set to German, Spanish or French, the registration heading, consent sentences, and sign-up block labels now appear in that language automatically. On video and gallery gates, the consent text also matches the page language; switching languages clears the previous consent sentence and tick so visitors must re-confirm in the new language.
entries.use_case: An organiser running a German-language event page no longer needs to manually override the registration heading or consent copy — they appear in German for every visitor without extra configuration.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A self-serve Marketing customer asks why their German or Spanish event page still shows English consent or registration labels.
internal.who_should_get_it: Self-serve Marketing customers whose event pages target German, Spanish or French audiences.
internal.gotchas: This change is gated to self-serve orgs. Platform orgs with a de/es/fr admin still receive English CSV headers and byte-identical English text — only the public-facing event page and gates are affected. The org-portal must be deployed after the matching web-api round-6 release; an older API rejects the new lng parameter.
internal.talk_track: Your German, Spanish and French visitors now see the registration form and consent copy in their own language — no manual overrides needed.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that event pages automatically render the registration heading, sign-up block labels and consent sentences in the page's configured language (de/es/fr), and that video and gallery gate consent resets when a visitor switches language.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Marketing event pages let you publish a branded registration and on-demand landing page without a separate website. When your audience speaks German, Spanish or French, the page — including the sign-up form labels and the consent text visitors must accept — renders in their language, so nothing looks out of place. Video and gallery gates follow the same rule: the consent sentence always matches the language the visitor is reading in, and switching languages resets the tick so consent is always given in the right language.

entries.title: Marketing Ask uses the shared chat experience — takeover, thread list and drawer
entries.summary: The **Ask** experience in Sessionboard Marketing now matches the other workspaces. Opening a chat — by typing in the Ask box, clicking a section tile, a recent chat, **Chats** or **New chat** — launches the full-screen **ChatTakeover**: a **Thread list** on the left (with setup pinned at the top showing its progress, then recent chats) and the conversation on the right. Close, Esc, the **Home** nav item or browser Back return to the Ask home page. The **Ask** drawer now opens with a **Chats** list and starts blank instead of reopening the last chat. All previously saved chats open exactly as before.
entries.use_case: Organizers who use Ask across Marketing, Learning and Awards now get the same thread list, takeover and keyboard navigation everywhere, so switching between workspaces feels consistent and saved chats are easy to find.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Marketing customer mentions that Ask feels different from Learning or Awards, or asks how to find a previous chat.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any customer using Sessionboard Marketing (beta) who uses Ask to plan or produce content.
internal.gotchas: Old ?thread= links in bookmarks or emails still work — they are silently rewritten to ?chat=. The conversation engine and all stored chat content are unchanged; only the navigation shell changed.
internal.talk_track: Ask in Marketing now has the same thread list and full-screen chat view as Learning and Awards, so your team can pick up any previous conversation right where they left it.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should document the ChatTakeover layout (thread list, New chat, Search chats, setup pinned with progress, Close / Esc to return home) and the drawer's Chats list, matching the depth of the Learning and Awards Ask guides.
draft.why_use_it: Ask in Sessionboard Marketing lets you plan, brief and execute your event marketing by describing what you want in plain language. The thread list keeps every conversation — from drafting a campaign brief to setting up your social plan — organised and easy to return to. Use it from the full-screen takeover when you want to focus, or from the drawer when you want to keep the rest of the page in view.

entries.title: Question-bank tags keep accented letters
entries.summary: Tags on question-bank questions now keep every letter: **Händehygiene** stays Händehygiene and **Réanimation** stays Réanimation, instead of losing their accented letters. A quiz that draws **Questions from the bank** by tag now finds questions tagged in any language. Separately, when you ask Ask about your learning data, it no longer says it can't see the data right above the card that shows it.
entries.use_case: A German or French association tags its question bank in its own language (Händehygiene, Réanimation) and draws quiz questions by those tags without them being renamed or missed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer tagging questions in German, French or Spanish says a tag lost its accented letters, or a bank draw found fewer questions than they tagged.
internal.who_should_get_it: Learning customers who keep a question bank in a language with accented letters.
internal.staff_path: Learning → Courses → open a course → Question bank
internal.gotchas: Tags saved before this change already lost their letters; re-tag those questions. English tags are unchanged. Stripe Connect code in the same PR has no admin UI and is not offered to customers (Josh, 2026-11-10): Learning sellers use Spreedly gateways or their own processor.
internal.talk_track: Tag your bank questions in your own language; the tags keep their accents and quizzes draw from them correctly.

draft.docs_gap: The question-bank guide can note that tags keep accented and non-Latin letters.
draft.why_use_it: A question bank lets you write a question once and reuse it across courses, and a quiz can draw a fresh set by tag on every attempt. Tags now keep accented letters, so organizations working in German, French or Spanish can tag in their own language and still draw exactly the questions they meant.

entries.title: Contract starter templates in German, French and Spanish
entries.summary: The three built-in contract starters — **Speaker Agreement**, **Sponsor Agreement** and **Exhibitor Agreement** — now appear in the workspace's language when the organization is set to German, French or Spanish. Names, descriptions, introductory text, clause sentences, the signature field label and the default email subject are all translated; template variables are unchanged. Organizations whose language is not de/fr/es continue to receive the English starters.
entries.use_case: A German or French association can now start from a ready-made agreement that reads in their own language, rather than having to rewrite an English starter before sending it to their speakers or sponsors.

cs_action.note: Starters are served automatically based on the org's language field; no action needed.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When onboarding a German, French or Spanish CRM customer who uses Contracts, or when an existing customer in those languages asks why their starters were in English.
internal.who_should_get_it: CRM customers whose organization language is set to de_DE, fr_FR or es_ES and who use the Contracts add-on.
internal.staff_path: CRM → Contracts → Templates (starter templates appear on first visit or when adding a starter)
internal.gotchas: If the org already added a starter in English, that existing copy is returned rather than a new translated one — no duplicates are created, but the existing template stays in English unless the customer edits it.
internal.talk_track: Your contract starters now come pre-written in German (or French or Spanish), so you can send a professional agreement to your speakers and sponsors without translating from English first.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that starter templates are served in the organization's language (German, French or Spanish) and that an existing English starter is not replaced or duplicated.
draft.why_use_it: Contract templates in Sessionboard CRM let you draft, send and collect e-signatures on speaker, sponsor and exhibitor agreements without leaving the platform. Starter templates give you a ready-made document for each relationship type that you can customise and publish in minutes. Signed copies are stored against each contact record so your team always knows who has agreed to what.

entries.title: See live watch progress while a lesson video plays
entries.summary: On a course with a watch-to-finish requirement, the **You've watched N%** line on a lesson now updates as the video plays, so learners see their real progress toward the requirement without reloading the page.
entries.use_case: A nurse who must watch 80% of a lesson before claiming credit sees the percentage climb as they watch, instead of a line stuck at 0% until they reload.

cs_action.note: Automatic for courses with a watch-to-finish requirement.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A learner says their watch percentage stayed at 0% while the video played.
internal.who_should_get_it: Learning customers who require watching a set share of a video before completion or credit.
internal.staff_path: Learning site → Course → Lesson with a required video
internal.gotchas: Needs lennd/sessionboard-web-api#5265 in production too; against an older API the line keeps the previous behaviour. The Stripe checkout code in the same PR is unreachable: Stripe Connect has no admin UI (Josh, 2026-11-10), so no Learning Site uses it.
internal.talk_track: Learners now see their watch percentage climb as the video plays, so they always know how close they are to credit.

draft.docs_gap: The what-learners-see guide can note that the watch percentage updates while the video plays.
draft.why_use_it: When a course requires watching a set share of a video before completion or credit, learners see their progress update as they watch, so they always know how close they are.

entries.title: Open in Clips appears on slide videos only when Clips is accessible
entries.summary: On the slide video editor, **Open in Clips** is shown only when your org and event have access to Clips. **Download MP4** and **Edit with chat** are always available regardless of your Clips access.
entries.use_case: Orgs without Clips access no longer see an Open in Clips button that leads nowhere; the button appears only when Clips is actually reachable for that org or event.

internal.when_to_bring_up: A customer reports that Open in Clips on a slide video redirected them to the Marketing overview or showed an error.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org using Slide Videos without the Clips feature enabled.
internal.staff_path: Marketing → Media → select a recording → Slide video
internal.gotchas: Open in Clips is hidden for orgs without the marketing flag or without marketing_clips on the event, and for org-level media routes without the media feature. Download MP4 and Edit with chat remain visible to everyone.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should note that Open in Clips appears only when the Clips feature is enabled for the org and event.

entries.title: Take notes, leave feedback, and share your certificate on LinkedIn from a Learning lesson
entries.summary: Learners on a Sessionboard Learning site can now write and save **Notes** while watching a lesson, submit anonymous or named **Feedback** after completing a lesson, and share their earned certificate directly to LinkedIn from the **Certificate** page. A **My Notes** page collects all notes across courses in one place.

where.path: Learning site → Lesson page / Certificate page / My Notes

entries.use_case: Learners who want to capture key takeaways while watching a lesson can jot notes without leaving the page, give the course team structured feedback when they finish, and post their certificate to LinkedIn to show professional development — all without leaving the learning site.

cs_action.note: All three features (notes, feedback, certificate share) are flag-gated under LEARNING_SIGNUP_ENABLED, which is off in prod. Nothing is live until the self-serve Learning release.

internal.when_to_bring_up: When a Learning customer asks how learners can engage more deeply with course content or share their achievements.
internal.who_should_get_it: Any org using Sessionboard Learning, especially professional associations offering CE credit or certification programs.
internal.staff_path: Learning site → Lesson page (Notes icon / Feedback tab) and Certificate page (Share to LinkedIn button)
internal.gotchas: Feedback can be set to anonymous, in which case organizers see responses but not names or dates. The flag LEARNING_SIGNUP_ENABLED must be on for the self-serve Learning site to be accessible; Platform Learning orgs will get these features on the prod release.
internal.talk_track: Your learners can now take notes right inside a lesson, give you feedback when they finish, and share their certificate on LinkedIn — making your courses stickier and your program more visible.

draft.docs_gap: The guide should add sections covering the Notes panel (writing, viewing, and the My Notes page), the post-lesson Feedback form (anonymous option), and the LinkedIn certificate share button.
draft.why_use_it: Sessionboard Learning gives your audience a branded place to take courses, earn credit, and prove what they have learned. Notes let learners build a personal study record as they go, lesson feedback gives your team direct input on course quality, and LinkedIn certificate sharing turns completions into visible professional credentials — helping you demonstrate the value of your education program.

entries.title: Start from what you came for, and add the rest when you need it
entries.summary: Your sidebar now opens on the job you signed up for, such as webinars, field events or clips. **Add more** opens **Add to Marketing**, with 13 things you can add: every one is on your plan, adding is free and removing deletes nothing. Ask can add them too: "Add Podcast to Marketing".
entries.use_case: A team that came for webinars sees webinars first, not ten menus, and adds a podcast or a newsletter in one click when it's ready, at no extra cost.
